To define $ \Delta S_{conf} $ we begin by comparing the adsorption of alkanes in five different zeolite structures: MFI, CHA, TON, FAU, and MOR. Depicted in Figure 2A is the relationship between the entropy of an adsorbed molecule (alkanes and permanent gases) and its gas-phase entropy, where the molecular entropy on the surface never exceeds that in the gas phase. While a significant loss in entropy occurs in all five zeolites, the absolute loss in entropy is distinct for each framework. Adsorbates in TON exhibit the largest loss in entropy upon adsorption, while FAU results in the smallest entropic losses. ABSTRACT: Confinement of hydrocarbons in nanoscale pockets and pores provides tunable capability for controlling molecules in catalysts, sorbents, and membranes for reaction and separation applications. While computation of the enthalpic interactions of hydrocarbons in confined spaces has improved, understanding and predicting the entropy of confined molecules remains a challenge. Here we show, using a set of nine aluminosilicate zeolite frameworks with broad variation in pore and cavity structure, that the entropy of adsorption can be predicted as a linear combination of rotational and translational entropy. The extent of entropy lost upon adsorption is predicted using only a single material descriptor, the occupiable volume ( $ V_{occ} $). Predictive capability of confined molecular entropy permits an understanding of the relation with adsorption enthalpy, the ability to computationally screen microporous materials, and an understanding of the role of confinement on the kinetics of molecules in confined spaces.

On the basis of this shape-selective feature , highly effective molecular separations and selective catalytic conversions can be achieved within zeolitic structures that are difficult to accomplish with other materials and/or techniques . $ ^ { 1-3 } $ So far, several shape-selectivity mechanisms have been elucidated and applications identified. $ ^{2-18} $ In common molecular sieving, bulky molecules adsorb preferentially over bulkier species as a result of steric constraints imposed by the zeolites' framework, e.g., linear alkane molecules compared to branched isomers. $ ^{19-23} $ Besides this common adsorption competition based on molecular bulkiness, the reverse phenomenon can also occur, i.e., competitive adsorption in favor of the bulkier species. Experiments revealed preferential adsorption of branched alkanes over their linear isomers on specific zeolites with tubular pore systems such as SAPO-5 and Mordenite. $ ^{24-28} $ Molecular simulations indicated that in such zeolites, depending on conditions, branched alkanes are preferentially adsorbed at the expense of linear isomers. $ ^{29-34} $ The present manuscript discusses the mechanisms of shape selectivity in n- and isoalkane adsorption on zeolite MCM-22. This zeolite with IZA code MWW is a relatively new synthetic material that has an unusual and quite complex pore structure. $ ^{35} $ Its framework is composed of two independent pore systems. The enthalpy and the entropy contributions to the Gibbs free energies were calculated at T = 298 K and partial pressure of 1 atm (101325 Pa). The enthalpy (H) of gas-phase pyridine and acetonitrile molecules is defined as the sum of total electronic energy ( $ E_{el} $), internal vibrational energy ( $ E_{v} $), zero-point vibrational energy (ZPVE), as well as the rotational and translational contributions to the internal energy: $ H = E_{el} + E_{v} + ZPVE + E_{R} + E_{t} $. The corresponding calculated entropies (S) includes translational, ( $ S_{t} $) vibrational, ( $ S_{v} $) and rotational ( $ S_{r} $) degrees of freedom: $ S = S_{t} + S_{v} + S_{r} $. All the considered systems are in singlet state, thus the electronic contribution to the entropy is zero. Since both adsorbed molecules are constrained in the zeolite cavity their entropy contributions in the adsorption complexes were corrected as follows: the translational and rotational degrees of freedom were reduced by 1 and 1.28 [37]. The Gibbs free energies of the zeolite support consist of only vibrational and electronic contributions. The expressions of all enthalpy and entropy contributions can be found in Ref. [38].

2.4.4. Trapdoor. Traditional diﬀusion models primarily consider two types of interactions: those between guest molecules (guest–guest) and those between guest molecules and the zeolite framework (guest–host). However, when cations are present in the zeolite structure, a third interaction—involving guest molecules, the framework, and cations (guest–host-cation)—must also be accounted for. A striking example of such ternary interactions is the well-known ‘‘molecular trapdoor’’. This phenomenon, also referred to as the ‘‘gating effect’’, describes a unique molecular sieving mechanism in certain zeolites and related porous materi- als. Here, extra-framework cations function as dynamic gate- keepers at pore apertures, selectively controlling molecular diffusion to achieve highly discriminative adsorption and separation.9,147,187 To date, ‘‘trapdoor’’ has been observed in several zeolites, including RHO (DNL-6),188–190 CHA (SAPO-34, SSZ-13),147,191,192 MWF (ZSM-25),149,193 HEU (Clinoptilolite),194

In the following appendix , we derive the entropy of adsorption in the case of infinite dilution and show how it may be related to familiar thermodynamic quantities ( cf . eq 5 ) . To begin , we define our adsorption entropy in the limit of infinite dilution via

$$ \Delta s_{\mathrm{ads}}^{\infty}=\lim_{N/V\rightarrow0}\left[\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{ads}}-\left(\frac{\partial S}{\partial N}\right)_{V,T,\mathrm{gas}}\right] $$

$$ =S_{ads}(N=1,V,T)-S_{gas}(N=1,V,T) $$

where the subscripts “ads” and “gas” labels identify the adsorbed (confined) and gas (bulk) phases, respectively. Given the constraints of a fixed number of molecules (N), volume (V), and temperature (T), it is natural to continue working in the canonical ensemble. (As in the main text, lowercase symbols identify intensive molecular or molar properties, whereas the uppercase indicates an extensive property.) For the molecules that we examine in this work (e.g., rigid molecules with no internal degrees of freedom), the canonical partition function Q may be expressed as

$$ \begin{aligned}Q(N,V,T)&=Q_{trans}(N,V,T)Q_{rot}(N,V,T)\\&\quad\times Z(N,V,T)\end{aligned} $$

where $ Q_{trans} $ and $ Q_{rot} $ are the translational and rotational partition functions (which are unaffected by confinement) and Z is the configurational partition function. The translational and rotational partition functions are available in the usual statistical mechanics texts $ ^{44,45} $ but are ultimately unimportant for the derivation that follows.

descriptor_candidates.name: confinement_ratio_descriptor
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(Vol) - log(AV * density) + log(0.7 + (lsd_p - PBF) / (lsd_p + PBF))
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: The entropy loss upon adsorption (ΔS/R) scales with the geometric mismatch between molecular free volume in the pore and the pore accessibility: adsorbates confined in pores whose accessible volume (Vol normalized by AV*density ratio) and pore-aperture-to-molecular-size ratio (lsd_p vs PBF) are tightly constrained lose a larger fraction of gas-phase entropy. Re-expressing confinement as a log-ratio of pore volume scale to accessible surface-normalized volume should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R relative to using raw occupiable volume alone (E02).
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Confined translational and rotational degrees of freedom are quenched proportional to the ratio of configurational phase-space volume in the pore to that in the gas phase (E01, E09). A tighter pore-to-molecule size match (smaller lsd_p - PBF relative to lsd_p + PBF) reduces accessible configurational microstates. This is inference from confinement partition-function arguments, not a verified new relation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If, on held-out zeolite/adsorbate pairs, the MAE of entropy loss/R using this descriptor is not lower than the MAE obtained using AV alone (the published single-descriptor baseline of E02), or if the descriptor's sign of correlation with entropy loss is reversed for small gases (CH4, Ar) versus alkanes, the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: asphericity_confinement_term
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(SPAN / GeDi) - log(1 + PMI3 / (PMI1 + 1e-8)) + log(1 + LabuteASA / (Vol ** (2.0/3.0) + 1e-8))
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss depends on the molecular shape anisotropy of the adsorbate interacting with the zeolite pore geometry: elongated or anisotropic molecules (high SPAN/GeDi ratio, high PMI3/PMI1 contrast) confined in small-pore frameworks (low lsd_f) experience greater rotational entropy quenching than isotropic molecules of equal volume, and this shape dependence is captured better by a combined asphericity-surface-to-volume descriptor than by volume alone.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Molecular shape selectivity in zeolites (E04) and differing rotational freedom under confinement (E01, E05) imply that rotational entropy loss is governed by how molecular principal-axis ratios interact with pore dimensionality. Surface-to-volume ratio (LabuteASA/Vol^(2/3)) captures the fraction of the molecule in contact with pore walls. This is a proposed new combination; the underlying shape-selectivity is known but the descriptor formula is not.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If the descriptor shows no improvement in MAE of entropy loss/R compared to Vol alone on held-out data, or if the coefficient of SPAN/GeDi is statistically indistinguishable from zero in a simple regression against the residual after removing the best volume-only model, the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: pore_accessibility_window_term
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(1 + ASA / (AV * density + 1e-8)) - log(1 + abs(lsd_f - lsd_p) / (lsd_f + lsd_p + 1e-8)) + log(1 + MW / (Vol + 1e-8))
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss increases with the ratio of framework-accessible surface area to pore volume (a confinement intensity measure) and decreases with the mismatch between the largest and smallest pore diameters (lsd_f vs lsd_p); denser, more strongly surface-bound configurations (higher MW/Vol) retain less gas-phase entropy. A descriptor built from these three ratios should predict entropy loss/R with lower MAE than any single geometric input.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: The ASA/AV ratio measures how much of the pore volume is close to a framework wall, which correlates with the number of quenched translational modes (E01, E09). The lsd_f/lsd_p mismatch captures pore heterogeneity: heterogeneous pore systems (e.g., MWW, E04) offer alternative adsorption sites and partially recover configurational entropy. Mass density (MW/Vol) is a proxy for the strength of host-guest contact and thus vibrational restriction. This combination is inferred, not established.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R using this descriptor does not decrease relative to a model using AV alone on the same held-out split, or if the descriptor systematically underestimates entropy loss for adsorbates in large-pore frameworks (FAU-like, E01) while overestimating for small-pore (TON-like), the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: window_gridlock_descriptor
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(1 + PBF / (lsd_f + 1e-8)) - log(1 + (lsd_f - lsd_p) / (lsd_f + lsd_p + 1e-8)) + log(1 + SPAN / (lsd_f + 1e-8))
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is governed by pore-window gridlock rather than by total pore volume: when the molecular longest dimension (PBF) approaches the framework-limiting window diameter (lsd_f), and the framework's window-size spread (lsd_f vs lsd_p) is small, the molecule loses more translational/rotational entropy than predicted by volume alone. The proposed descriptor should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R below the current best (0.5569) and improve over the retained confinement_ratio_descriptor.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from configurational partition-function arguments (E09) and shape selectivity (E04): the aperture, not the cavity, sets the number of accessible configurational microstates. Molecules whose longest axis (SPAN, PBF) approaches the smallest window (lsd_f) in a spatially anisotropic zeolite are forced into few orientational states. Framework flexibility (E06, E10) may relax this constraint, which is why lsd_f - lsd_p enters as a corrective term. This is a proposed recombination, not an established relation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R on the held-out split is not lower than 0.5569 (retained round-1 descriptor), or if residual correlation of the descriptor with entropy loss is dominated by Vol (i.e., the descriptor adds no information beyond volume), the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: surface_contact_compaction_descriptor
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(1 + ASA * LabuteASA / (AV * density * Vol + 1e-8)) + log(1 + GeDi / (lsd_p + 1e-8)) - log(1 + MW / 100.0)
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss scales with the intensity of molecule-framework wall contact per unit of accessible free volume: frameworks with high specific surface area per accessible pore volume (ASA relative to AV*density) combined with molecules of high contact area-to-volume ratio (LabuteASA/Vol) lose more entropy, while heavier molecules (higher MW) partially compensate by dispersing contact over more atoms. The descriptor should outperform the round-1 best on MAE of entropy loss/R and show a monotonic positive partial correlation with entropy loss across zeolite frameworks including both FAU-like (small loss) and TON-like (large loss) systems.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: E01 and E09 show that adsorbed entropy never exceeds gas-phase entropy and the loss varies systematically with framework; E09's configurational partition function implies that the fraction of molecular configuration space lying near framework walls controls the entropy reduction. The product ASA * LabuteASA / (free volume proxy) is a contact-intensity measure; GeDi/lsd_p tests whether molecular gyration-diameter relative to pore diameter modulates residual configurational freedom. The MW term is an inference, marked uncertain in mechanism.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R does not improve on 0.5569, or if the descriptor overestimates entropy loss for small permanent gases (Ar, CH4, per E01) while underestimating it for alkanes (sign reversal across adsorbate classes), the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: moment_inertia_pore_phase_descriptor
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(1 + (PMI1 + PMI2) / (PMI3 + 1e-8)) - log(1 + abs(PBF - lsd_p) / (PBF + lsd_p + 1e-8)) + log(1 + LabuteASA / (MW + 1e-8))
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Rotational entropy loss is controlled by the rotational degeneracy contrast of the molecule: near-spherical or prolate molecules (low PMI1+PMI2 relative to PMI3 contrast, i.e., high ratio) retain more rotational freedom under confinement than oblate or highly anisotropic molecules, and this effect is modulated by how closely the molecular size (PBF) matches the pore diameter (lsd_p) and by surface contact per unit mass (LabuteASA/MW). The descriptor should yield lower MAE of entropy loss/R than the round-1 best and specifically improve accuracy for anisotropic adsorbates (long-chain alkanes, aromatics).
descriptor_candidates.rationale: E01 documents that rotational entropy contributions are a significant, framework-dependent fraction of total gas-phase entropy lost; E07 shows molecular symmetry affects dynamics under confinement. Inference: the rotational partition function inside a pore is truncated by the ratio of accessible orientations, which depends on principal-moment contrast and on aperture-to-size matching (E04, E10). The LabuteASA/MW term proxies wall contact per unit of rotational mass. Combination is proposed, not established.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R does not improve on 0.5569 on the held-out split, or if the descriptor fails to improve the anisotropic-adsorbate subset (SPAN > median SPAN) relative to the isotropic subset (no differential MAE reduction), the hypothesis is falsified.

candidates.formula: log(1 + ASA * LabuteASA / (AV * density * Vol + 1e-8)) + log(1 + GeDi / (lsd_p + 1e-8)) - log(1 + MW / 100.0)
candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss scales with the intensity of molecule-framework wall contact per unit of accessible free volume: frameworks with high specific surface area per accessible pore volume (ASA relative to AV*density) combined with molecules of high contact area-to-volume ratio (LabuteASA/Vol) lose more entropy, while heavier molecules (higher MW) partially compensate by dispersing contact over more atoms. The descriptor should outperform the round-1 best on MAE of entropy loss/R and show a monotonic positive partial correlation with entropy loss across zeolite frameworks including both FAU-like (small loss) and TON-like (large loss) systems.
candidates.rationale: E01 and E09 show that adsorbed entropy never exceeds gas-phase entropy and the loss varies systematically with framework; E09's configurational partition function implies that the fraction of molecular configuration space lying near framework walls controls the entropy reduction. The product ASA * LabuteASA / (free volume proxy) is a contact-intensity measure; GeDi/lsd_p tests whether molecular gyration-diameter relative to pore diameter modulates residual configurational freedom. The MW term is an inference, marked uncertain in mechanism.
candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R does not improve on 0.5569, or if the descriptor overestimates entropy loss for small permanent gases (Ar, CH4, per E01) while underestimating it for alkanes (sign reversal across adsorbate classes), the hypothesis is falsified.

candidates.name: moment_inertia_pore_phase_descriptor
candidates.formula: log(1 + (PMI1 + PMI2) / (PMI3 + 1e-8)) - log(1 + abs(PBF - lsd_p) / (PBF + lsd_p + 1e-8)) + log(1 + LabuteASA / (MW + 1e-8))
candidates.hypothesis: Rotational entropy loss is controlled by the rotational degeneracy contrast of the molecule: near-spherical or prolate molecules (low PMI1+PMI2 relative to PMI3 contrast, i.e., high ratio) retain more rotational freedom under confinement than oblate or highly anisotropic molecules, and this effect is modulated by how closely the molecular size (PBF) matches the pore diameter (lsd_p) and by surface contact per unit mass (LabuteASA/MW). The descriptor should yield lower MAE of entropy loss/R than the round-1 best and specifically improve accuracy for anisotropic adsorbates (long-chain alkanes, aromatics).
candidates.rationale: E01 documents that rotational entropy contributions are a significant, framework-dependent fraction of total gas-phase entropy lost; E07 shows molecular symmetry affects dynamics under confinement. Inference: the rotational partition function inside a pore is truncated by the ratio of accessible orientations, which depends on principal-moment contrast and on aperture-to-size matching (E04, E10). The LabuteASA/MW term proxies wall contact per unit of rotational mass. Combination is proposed, not established.
candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R does not improve on 0.5569 on the held-out split, or if the descriptor fails to improve the anisotropic-adsorbate subset (SPAN > median SPAN) relative to the isotropic subset (no differential MAE reduction), the hypothesis is falsified.

rounds.retained_formula: log(1 + PBF / (lsd_f + 1e-8)) - log(1 + (lsd_f - lsd_p) / (lsd_f + lsd_p + 1e-8)) + log(1 + SPAN / (lsd_f + 1e-8))

descriptor_candidates.name: rotational_channel_compatibility_descriptor
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(1 + (PMI3 / (PMI1 + 1e-8)) ** 0.5) - log(1 + abs(lsd_p - GeDi) / (lsd_p + GeDi + 1e-8)) + log(1 + lsd_f / (SPAN + 1e-8))
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss is governed by the compatibility between molecular rotational geometry and channel dimensionality: molecules with large principal-moment contrast (PMI3/PMI1, e.g., linear chains) confined in pores whose diameter (lsd_p, lsd_f) matches their gyration diameter (GeDi) and longest extent (SPAN) lose more rotational entropy than isotropic molecules of equal volume, because only a subset of orientational states fits through and within the channel. The descriptor should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R below the current best 0.5338 and specifically reduce error on the anisotropic-adsorbate subset.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from rotational partition-function truncation under confinement (E01, E09): the adsorbed rotational partition function is a restricted integral over orientations, whose volume shrinks when the molecular inertia ellipsoid (PMI1, PMI3; GeDi, SPAN) fills the pore cross-section (lsd_p, lsd_f). Shape selectivity of zeolites (E04) supports aperture-dependent orientational restriction. Framework flexibility (E06, E10) may soften the constraint, so pore-size terms enter as ratios rather than hard cutoffs. This is a proposed recombination, not an established relation.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R on the held-out split does not improve on 0.5338, or if the descriptor does not differentially improve the anisotropic subset (SPAN above median) relative to the isotropic subset, the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: free_volume_dilution_descriptor
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(1 + Vol / (AV * density * MW + 1e-8)) + log(1 + PBF * LabuteASA / (Vol + 1e-8)) - log(1 + (lsd_f + lsd_p) / (2.0 * PBF + 1e-8))
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: The fraction of gas-phase entropy retained upon adsorption is controlled by the per-mass dilution of free volume and the molecule's wall-contact fraction: frameworks where occupiable volume per unit mass per unit adsorbate size is small force the molecule into a narrow configurational subspace, while a high contact-area-to-volume ratio (PBF * LabuteASA / Vol) increases the quenched surface-proximal modes; large windows relative to molecular size (lsd_f + lsd_p vs 2*PBF) partially restore configurational freedom. The descriptor should yield MAE of entropy loss/R below 0.5338 and remain accurate across both FAU-like (small loss) and TON-like (large loss) frameworks.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from the configurational partition function at infinite dilution (E09): entropy loss reflects the ratio of the pore-accessible configurational volume to the gas-phase translational volume, which scales inversely with mass (Sackur-Tetrode, E01). Free volume per adsorbate mass (Vol / (AV*density*MW)) is a phase-space dilution proxy; the contact-fraction term proxies the fraction of configurations quenched by proximity to walls; the window-to-size term captures residual escape/orientational freedom softened by framework flexibility (E06, E10). Proposed combination, not established.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R does not improve on 0.5338, or if the descriptor systematically overestimates entropy loss for small permanent gases (Ar, CH4) and underestimates it for long alkanes (sign reversal across adsorbate classes per E01), the hypothesis is falsified.

descriptor_candidates.name: aperture_throughput_descriptor
descriptor_candidates.formula: log(1 + PBF / (lsd_f + 1e-8)) - log(1 + SPAN / (lsd_p + 1e-8)) + log(1 + density * AV / (Vol + 1e-8)) - log(1 + abs(PMI2 - PMI1) / (PMI3 + 1e-8))
descriptor_candidates.hypothesis: Entropy loss depends on aperture throughput asymmetry rather than on cavity volume: when the molecular minimum cross-section (proxied by PMI2 vs PMI1 near-degeneracy for rods) dictates passage through windows (lsd_f), while the longest dimension (SPAN) is accommodated by the pore (lsd_p), adsorbates in frameworks with high framework compactness (density*AV per occupiable volume) lose more entropy because orientational sampling is restricted to a narrow passage cone. The descriptor should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R below 0.5338 and outperform the retained window_gridlock_descriptor on branched/compact adsorbates.
descriptor_candidates.rationale: Inference from molecular sieving and shape selectivity (E04): passage through windows is governed by the minimum cross-section, not the maximum extent, so principal-moment contrast (PMI2 vs PMI1 relative to PMI3) controls whether molecules thread windows with little or large orientational restriction (E07 shows symmetry-dependent confined dynamics). The compactness term (density*AV/Vol) measures how much of the framework is wall versus void. Framework vibration and flexibility (E10, E06) allow slight oversize passage, motivating soft log-ratios. Proposed combination, not established.
descriptor_candidates.falsification_criteria: If MAE of entropy loss/R on the held-out split is not lower than 0.5338, or if the descriptor adds no information beyond the retained window_gridlock_descriptor (no residual correlation improvement after removing it, and no differential gain on compact/branched adsorbates), the hypothesis is falsified.

retained.name: confinement_ratio_descriptor
retained.formula: log(Vol) - log(AV * density) + log(0.7 + (lsd_p - PBF) / (lsd_p + PBF))
retained.hypothesis: The entropy loss upon adsorption (ΔS/R) scales with the geometric mismatch between molecular free volume in the pore and the pore accessibility: adsorbates confined in pores whose accessible volume (Vol normalized by AV*density ratio) and pore-aperture-to-molecular-size ratio (lsd_p vs PBF) are tightly constrained lose a larger fraction of gas-phase entropy. Re-expressing confinement as a log-ratio of pore volume scale to accessible surface-normalized volume should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R relative to using raw occupiable volume alone (E02).

retained.name: window_gridlock_descriptor
retained.formula: log(1 + PBF / (lsd_f + 1e-8)) - log(1 + (lsd_f - lsd_p) / (lsd_f + lsd_p + 1e-8)) + log(1 + SPAN / (lsd_f + 1e-8))
retained.hypothesis: Entropy loss is governed by pore-window gridlock rather than by total pore volume: when the molecular longest dimension (PBF) approaches the framework-limiting window diameter (lsd_f), and the framework's window-size spread (lsd_f vs lsd_p) is small, the molecule loses more translational/rotational entropy than predicted by volume alone. The proposed descriptor should reduce MAE of entropy loss/R below the current best (0.5569) and improve over the retained confinement_ratio_descriptor.
